titulo: Stare + gerundio, stare per, appena: Stare per and appena

aula.objetivo: Say what is happening now and what was in progress with «stare» and the gerundio, say what is about to happen with «stare per», and use «appena», «tra poco» and «da poco». Avoid the English-speaker traps: using «essere» instead of «stare», using the infinitive instead of the gerundio, and using the progressive for plans.

itens.pt: I am about to go out

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «stare per» + infinitive means «to be about to»: «Sto per uscire» (I am about to go out), «Il treno sta per partire» (the train is about to leave). It speaks of something that will happen in a moment. STEP 2: use the infinitive, not the gerundio: «sta per piovere», not «sta per piovendo». STEP 3: «appena» has two main uses. Inside the passato prossimo it means «just»: «Ho appena finito» (I have just finished), with the word between the auxiliary and the participle. STEP 4: choose the auxiliary as usual: «Sono appena arrivato» (arrivare takes «essere»), «Ho appena mangiato». STEP 5: at the start of a clause, «appena» means «as soon as»: «Appena arrivo, ti aiuto» (As soon as I arrive, I will help you). It can also open a clause in the past («Appena sono arrivato, ho chiamato»). STEP 6: «tra poco» (or «fra poco») looks to the future: «Ci vediamo tra poco» (we will see each other in a little while). STEP 7: «da poco» looks back: «Abito qui da poco» (I have lived here for a short time) and «Sono arrivato da poco» (I arrived a short time ago). STEP 8: do not confuse them: «tra poco» is ahead of now, «da poco» is behind it.
blocos.comparacao: English «about to» matches «stare per» well, and both are followed by the bare infinitive: «about to leave» and «sto per partire». The «be» trap returns: English «is about to» uses «be», but Italian uses «stare»: «è per partire» is wrong. «Just» in English is a separate word before the participle («I have just left»); Italian also puts «appena» before the participle, between the auxiliary and the participle. And English uses different phrases for ahead and behind («in a little while», «a short time ago»); Italian changes only the small word: «tra poco» (ahead), «da poco» (behind).

exemplos.pt: I am about to go out
The train is about to leave

tabela.forma: sto per uscire · sta per piovere
ho appena finito · sono appena arrivato

erros.motivo: «Arrivare» takes «essere», and «appena» keeps its place between auxiliary and participle.
After «per» use the infinitive («piovere»), not the gerundio.

itens.enunciado: Which sentence means «The train is about to leave»?
